The '''Exploit Prediction Scoring System''' ('''EPSS''') is a [[technical standard]] managed by [[Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams|FIRST]] for estimating the probability a publicly disclosed software [[Vulnerability (computer security)|vulnerability]] will be [[Exploit (computer security)|exploited]] in the wild within the next 30 days.<ref name="FIRST2025">{{cite web |title=EPSS Version 4 Released |url=https://www.first.org/epss/ |website=FIRST |date=17 March 2025 |access-date=14 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kovacs |first=Eduard |date=2025-05-20 |title=Vulnerability Exploitation Probability Metric Proposed by NIST, CISA Researchers |url=https://www.securityweek.com/vulnerability-exploitation-probability-metric-proposed-by-nist-cisa-researchers/ |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=SecurityWeek |language=en-US}}</ref> EPSS is complementary to the [[Common Vulnerability Scoring System]].<ref name="FIRST2025" /> Combining EPSS and CVSS aligns remediation with actual threat activity.<ref name="Jiang">{{cite arXiv |title=A Survey on Vulnerability Prioritization: Taxonomy, Metrics, and Challenges |date=12 February 2025 |eprint=2502.11070 |last1=Jiang |first1=Yuning |last2=Oo |first2=Nay |last3=Meng |first3=Qiaoran |author4=Hoon Wei Lim |last5=Sikdar |first5=Biplab |class=cs.CR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ravalico |first=Damiano |last2=Farina |first2=Mauro |last3=Trevisan |first3=Martino |last4=Bartoli |first4=Alberto |date=2025 |title=Analysing the Temporal Dynamics of the Exploit Prediction Scoring Systems (Epss) |url=https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5147459 |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=doi.org}}</ref>

== Characteristics ==
Vulnerabilities get assigned a [[probability]] value between 0 and 1 that determines the chance of them being exploited in the real world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) Special Interest Group (SIG) |url=https://www.first.org/epss/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=FIRST — Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
The original concept and prototype were presented by researchers Michael Roytman, Jay Jacobs, and Sasha Romanosky at [[Black Hat (conference)|Black Hat]] in 2019.<ref name="Brinqa">{{cite web |title=What Is an EPSS Score? |url=https://www.brinqa.com/glossary/what-is-epss-score/ |website=Brinqa |date=10 February 2024 |access-date=14 April 2025}}</ref> In April 2020 FIRST started a [[special interest group]] to develop the standard.<ref name="EPSSSIG">{{cite web |title=EPSS Special Interest Group Portal |url=https://portal.first.org/g/epss-sig |website=FIRST |access-date=14 April 2025}}</ref>

=== Versions ===
* 7 January 2021 – Public publication of daily EPSS scores began (model v1).<ref name="FOSSA2023v1">{{cite web |title=Understanding and Using the EPSS Scoring System |url=https://fossa.com/blog/understanding-using-epss-scoring-system/ |website=FOSSA Blog |date=20 January 2023 |access-date=14 April 2025}}</ref>
* 4 February 2022 – Version 2 incorporated additional telemetry sources and algorithmic improvements.
* 7 March 2023 – Version 3 introduced gradient-boosted decision trees and expanded feature sets.
* 17 March 2025 – Version 4 added contextual threat-intelligence feeds and performance gains.<ref name="FIRST2025" />

== Adoption ==
The U.S. [[Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency]] (CISA) encourages using EPSS alongside its [[Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog]] for patch triage.<ref name="Parla">{{cite arXiv |last=Parla |first=Rianna |title=Efficacy of EPSS in High Severity CVEs Found in CISA KEV |date=4 November 2024 |class=cs.CR |eprint=2411.02618}}</ref> Major vulnerability-management platforms, such as Rapid7, Tenable, and Qualys, integrate EPSS scores for risk-based patching.<ref name="Brinqa" /> Academic research uses EPSS to model exploit trends and evaluate defenses.<ref name="Mell">{{cite arXiv |title=Measuring the Exploitation of Weaknesses in the Wild |date=1 May 2024 |eprint=2405.01289 |last1=Mell |first1=Peter |last2=Bojanova |first2=Irena |last3=Galhardo |first3=Carlos |class=cs.CR}}</ref>
